parameters.input_path_note: Uploaded asset used (declared default /app/assets/healthcare_hiring_900.csv was not present); this is the healthcare hiring dataset with the schema specified in the runbook.

data_quality.missing_demographic_data: none -- gender, race_ethnicity, disability_status, veteran_status, age all fully populated for all 900 rows
data_quality.only_missing_column: certifications (167 blanks = 'no certifications listed'), not used in disparity calculation

stages.name: data_loading
stages.message: 900 rows loaded and validated; 0 rows dropped; age_bracket derived

stages.name: aggregation
stages.message: 125 disparity metric rows computed across 6 roles + ALL_ROLES rollup x 5 dimensions

stages.name: summary_accuracy_validation
stages.message: summary.md flagged-count (24) and top-5 severity list verified against disparity_metrics.csv on round 1

rate_bounds.note: 33 low_confidence rows have four_fifths_ratio > 1.0 because the reference group is restricted to candidate_count>=30 cells; a small excluded group can by chance have a higher raw selection rate than that size-restricted reference. All 33 are confirmed low_confidence=true. This is expected per the methodology's own eligibility rule (see runbook Tips), not a calculation defect, and is not counted as a violation.

statistical_rigor.notes: Both Fisher's exact and Yates-corrected chi-square computed for every cell with candidate_count>=30 on both sides (verified: dual_test_presence check found 0 violations). statistically_significant confirmed programmatically to equal fisher_significant AND chi2_significant for all 125 rows (significance_combination_rule check: 0 violations). 16 of 24 flagged rows are clearly marked low_confidence and distinguished from the 3 adequately-powered significant findings in report Sections 3-4.

completeness_of_breakdowns.notes: All 6 job roles have a dedicated findings subsection (Section 2) and all 5 requested protected attributes (gender, race_ethnicity, disability_status, veteran_status, age_bracket) appear in both the per-role breakdown and the ALL_ROLES cross-role rollup table (Section 3).

clarity_of_findings.notes: Section 3 rollup table and Section 4 flagged-items table cite exact selection rates, four-fifths ratios, and both fisher_p_value and chi2_p_value inline for every row where they apply -- no cross-referencing of the CSV needed to judge severity.

actionability_of_recommendations.notes: Section 5 has 6 recommendations, each naming a specific role/group/metric (e.g. 'Registered Nurse hiring by age bracket', 'Pharmacist role generally') and explicitly labeled as investigate-further vs. collect-more-data vs. review-process vs. no-action.

appropriate_caveats_and_tone.notes: Section 6 explicitly separates statistical disparity from proof of discrimination, explicitly caveats the 16 low-confidence flagged cells, and notes the synthetic/non-legal nature of the audit. Language throughout uses 'statistical disparity was observed' framing rather than assertions of bias.

factual_self_consistency.notes: Pre-scoring verification (required by Step 6) recomputed true_flagged_count=24 directly from disparity_metrics.csv, matching the report's stated count exactly. The true top-5-by-severity (sorted by four_fifths_ratio ascending, tie-broken by statistically_significant then low_confidence) was recomputed and found to be exactly the 5 rows the report surfaces first in Section 4 (rows 1-5: Medical Coder Middle Eastern, Medical Coder Multiracial, Registered Nurse Multiracial, Pharmacist Black, Pharmacist Middle Eastern). Spot-checked one ratio + both p-values per protected attribute dimension (gender/Female, race_ethnicity/Hispanic-Latino & Multiracial, disability_status/Yes, veteran_status/No, age_bracket/30-39) against the CSV -- all matched to reported precision. Zero discrepancies found in the first draft, so no correction cycle was needed.
